- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.12 to +0.61); model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 to -0.22) or after a recent dip; model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction — especially in 30-day forecasts.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for downward pressure.
- If recent 18-day history shows a sharp upward move followed by a dip, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 3–7% in next 5–7 days.
- Forecast should be adjusted downward if sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment scores).
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile — use 18-day history as a smoother anchor for correction.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If model forecast is <10% below recent 18-day average, increase by 3–7% if sentiment is positive or neutral.
